# libtmux for Raku
LibTmux controls tmux from Raku: create sessions and panes, find them through typed snapshots, send input, and react to terminal output. Use ordinary Raku predicates and collections alongside validated query data and explicit commands. ## Install Requires Linux, Raku 6.d and tmux 3.3a through 3.8. Install the published package from [Raku Land](https://raku.land/zef:libtmux/LibTmux) with its Fez authority: ```console $ zef install 'LibTmux:auth' ``` The API is experimental and may change between `0.x` releases. CI qualifies Rakudo 2026.09 on Linux with tmux 3.3a and 3.8; other platforms and compiler versions are unverified. See the [changelog][repo-changelog-md] for release history. The [toolchain guide][repo-github-contributing-md-toolchain] covers Raku and zef setup. To install a checkout instead: ```console $ zef install . ``` ## Create sessions and panes ### [`Server.start`][api-server-start] and [`PaneRef.split`][api-pane-split]: create and arrange panes Create a private tmux session named `work`, split its first pane, and set the pane titles to `editor` and `logs`. Both panes run `cat` as an echo process. This is the complete [quickstart program][repo-examples-quickstart-raku]. `LEAVE` closes the owned server when the program exits, including on an exception. ```raku use LibTmux; my $server = Server.start(:name, :shell-command('exec cat')); LEAVE $server.close if $server.defined; my $before = $server.snapshot; my $left = $before.panes.single.ref; my $right = $left.split(:horizontal, :shell-command('exec cat')); $left.set-title('editor'); $right.set-title('logs'); my $after = $server.snapshot; my $editor = $after.panes.filter(*.title eq 'editor').single; say "{$editor.title}: {$after.panes.elems} panes"; ``` It prints `editor: 2 panes`. The earlier snapshot still contains one pane: commands through `.ref` change tmux, while snapshots retain the state they captured. Reading a snapshot or following its relationships makes no further tmux calls. Run it from the checkout with a supported tmux executable on `PATH`: ```console $ raku -I. examples/quickstart.raku ``` ## Query captured panes ### [`PaneSelection.where`][api-pane-selection-where]: select panes from a snapshot Create panes titled `editor`, `tests`, and `logs`. Select wide panes with query data, then use a Raku predicate to find `editor`. The complete [query program][repo-examples-query-panes-raku] also uses native `.grep`, `.map` and `.sort` to list the other panes. ```raku use v6.d; use LibTmux; sub MAIN(Str:D :$tmux = 'tmux') { my $server = Server.start(:binary($tmux), :name, :width(160), :height(40), :shell-command('exec cat')); LEAVE $server.close if $server.defined; my $editor = $server.snapshot.panes.single.ref; my $tests = $editor.split(:horizontal, :shell-command('exec cat')); my $logs = $tests.split(:shell-command('exec cat')); $editor.set-title('editor'); $tests.set-title('tests'); $logs.set-title('logs'); my $snapshot = $server.snapshot; my @wide := $snapshot.panes.where(%(width => %(gte => 60))); my $selected = @wide.filter(*.title eq 'editor').single; say "Wide pane: {$selected.title}"; my @others = $snapshot.panes.grep(*.id ne $selected.id).map(*.title).sort; say 'Other panes: ' ~ @others.join(', '); } ``` It prints `Wide pane: editor` and `Other panes: logs, tests`. Binding with `:=` retains the typed selection. [`where`][api-pane-selection-where] validates query fields and operators; [`filter`][api-pane-selection-filter] returns another selection of the same entity type. Native `.grep` returns a `Seq`, and `.map` can produce ordinary strings. `.single` requires exactly one result; `.single-or-nil` permits no result. Raku's `.one` keeps its junction meaning. For live acquisition, [`query-panes(:where(%criteria))`][api-server-query-panes] returns a fresh selection. [`explain-panes`][api-server-explain-panes] shows which restrictions run in tmux and which remain local. See the [native query guide][repo-lib-libtmux-rakumod] for relations, portable filters and source execution. ## Adapt to the running daemon ### [`Capabilities.supports`][api-capabilities-supports]: choose a supported operation Create an empty `status` pane as a floating pane when supported, with a tiled split as the fallback. The [capability example][repo-examples-floating-panes-raku] asks the captured daemon capabilities before choosing an operation. ```raku use v6.d; use LibTmux; sub MAIN(Str:D :$tmux = 'tmux') { my $server = Server.start(:binary($tmux), :name, :width(120), :height(36), :shell-command('exec cat')); LEAVE $server.close if $server.defined; my $snapshot = $server.snapshot; my $main = $snapshot.panes.single.ref; my $floating = $snapshot.capabilities.supports('pane-floating'); my $auxiliary = $floating ?? $main.new-floating(:width(40), :height(12), :x(2), :y(2), :empty) !! $main.split(:horizontal, :empty); $auxiliary.set-title('status'); my $after = $server.snapshot; die 'The auxiliary pane was not captured' unless $after.panes.elems == 2; say 'Status pane: ' ~ ($floating ?? 'floating' !! 'tiled'); say $after.panes.where(%(id => $auxiliary.id)).single.title; } ``` It prints `Status pane: floating` or `Status pane: tiled`, followed by `status`. A newer client executable does not upgrade an older daemon. Unknown releases are refused conservatively. The [compatibility policy][repo-docs-adr-0001-tmux-compatibility-md] describes support; the [field and capability reference][repo-docs-reference-catalogue-rakudoc] lists feature requirements and unavailable values. ## Watch pane output ### [`ControlConnection.events`][api-connection-events]: receive output through a `Supply` Asynchronous operations return `Promise` values. A control connection exposes events through a shared `Supply`; native `react` and `whenever` consume them. [`Server.open-control-async`][api-server-open-control-async] opens the connection. This complete [output watcher][repo-examples-watch-output-raku] subscribes before sending text to `cat`, waits for the echoed bytes, then checks the captured screen. ```raku use v6.d; use LibTmux; use LibTmux::Control; sub MAIN(Str:D :$tmux = 'tmux') { my $server = Server.start(:binary($tmux), :name, :shell-command('exec cat')); LEAVE $server.close if $server.defined; my $snapshot = await $server.snapshot-async; my $pane = $snapshot.panes.single.ref; my $connection = await $server.open-control-async(:session-id($snapshot.sessions.single.id)); LEAVE $connection.close if $connection.defined; my $message = 'hello from Raku'; my $received = ''; react { whenever $connection.events.grep(PaneOutput) -> $event { if $event.pane-id eq $pane.id { $received ~= $event.data.decode('utf8-c8'); die 'Pane output exceeded its bound' if $received.chars > 65536; done if $received.contains($message); } } whenever start { $pane.send-text($message); $pane.send-keys('Enter') } { } whenever Promise.in(2) { die 'Pane output timed out' } } die 'The captured screen did not contain the message' unless $pane.capture.decode('utf8').contains($message); say $message; say 'Screen capture confirmed'; } ``` It prints `hello from Raku` and `Screen capture confirmed`. The deadline bounds the wait; output events supply the completion evidence. `send-text` sends literal text, and `send-keys('Enter')` submits it separately. Pane output arrives as bytes so fragmented or invalid UTF-8 remains available. The longer [session workflow program][repo-examples-session-workflow-raku] combines pane creation, output observation, capture, local queries and an explained source query in one lifecycle. ## Recover after a batch fails ### [`Server.run-batch`][api-server-run-batch]: inspect partial completion A batch records each operation's outcome. The [recovery program][repo-examples-batch-recovery-raku] produces `Complete`, `Failed` and `Skipped`, verifies that the first effect remains, then removes that effect explicitly. Command acknowledgement alone does not establish application completion, and a failed batch does not roll back earlier commands. ```console $ raku -I. examples/batch-recovery.raku ``` The [examples guide][repo-examples-readme-md] gives the commands, expected results and cleanup behavior for every complete program. ## Ownership and documentation ### [`Server.close`][api-server-close]: close an owned daemon [`Server.start`][api-server-start] creates and owns a daemon on a private socket. [`Server.new`][api-server-new] configures a borrowed endpoint; closing it leaves that daemon running. Close both explicitly. Control connections and terminal attachments have their own lifetimes and also need closing. References are scoped to the observed daemon incarnation and refuse a replacement daemon. API links open the native declarations and their RakuDoc comments. - [Native API guide][repo-lib-libtmux-rakumod]: the object graph, queries, capabilities, async execution, control events and recovery. - [Examples][repo-examples-readme-md]: complete Raku programs with checked results. - [Contributing][repo-github-contributing-md]: compiler setup and validation. - [API documentation authoring][repo-docs-documentation-rakudoc] and [writing conventions][repo-github-writing-md]. - [MIT license][repo-license] and [artwork provenance][repo-docs-assets-readme-md]. # libtmux Raku examples
Create sessions, split panes, watch terminal output, and recover a failed command. These complete Raku programs use [LibTmux](../README.md) to own private tmux servers. Each closes its clients and daemon when it exits. Run commands from the repository root after the [toolchain setup](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#toolchain), with a supported tmux executable on `PATH`: ```console $ zef install . ``` | Task | Program | Raku facilities | | --- | --- | --- | | Create and find panes | [Quickstart](quickstart.raku) | Objects, `LEAVE`, a native predicate | | Select wide panes | [Pane queries](query-panes.raku) | Typed selections, query hashes, `grep`, `map`, `sort` | | Add a status pane | [Floating panes](floating-panes.raku) | Capability checks and a tiled fallback | | Watch pane output | [Watch output](watch-output.raku) | `Promise`, `Supply`, `react`, `whenever` | | Combine the workflow | [Session workflow](session-workflow.raku) | Events, captured graphs and query plans | | Recover after a command fails | [Batch recovery](batch-recovery.raku) | Typed outcomes and explicit recovery | ## Create and find panes The [quickstart](quickstart.raku) is the complete first program in the root README. It creates two panes, sets their titles, and finds the editor pane through a fresh snapshot. The earlier snapshot retains one pane. ```console $ raku -I. examples/quickstart.raku ``` It prints `editor: 2 panes`. ## Select wide panes The [pane query program](query-panes.raku) creates panes titled `editor`, `tests`, and `logs`. `.where` selects the wide panes, `.filter` finds `editor`, and `.single` checks cardinality. Native `.grep`, `.map` and `.sort` produce the remaining pane names as ordinary Raku values. ```console $ raku -I. examples/query-panes.raku ``` It prints `Wide pane: editor` and `Other panes: logs, tests`. Use `:=` when binding a typed selection to an array variable. Assignment with `=` materializes ordinary array membership. Repeated traversal reads the captured members; it does not refresh tmux. ## Add a status pane The [floating-pane program](floating-panes.raku) creates an empty `status` pane. It checks the daemon's `pane-floating` capability, chooses a floating pane when available, and otherwise splits the tiled window. ```console $ raku -I. examples/floating-panes.raku ``` It prints the selected placement, then `status`. The empty display has no child process on profiles that report an absent PID; the pane still belongs to the captured graph. Consult capabilities before offering an operation to a user. ## Watch pane output The [output watcher](watch-output.raku) awaits asynchronous snapshot and control connection operations, subscribes to pane-output events, and sends text to `cat` as an echo process. `react` and `whenever` collect fragmented bytes until the complete message arrives. It then checks the captured screen. ```console $ raku -I. examples/watch-output.raku ``` It prints `hello from Raku` and `Screen capture confirmed`. The deadline bounds the wait. Multiple event subscribers share the same owned connection. Sending text and pressing Enter are separate operations. ## Run the complete session workflow The [session workflow](session-workflow.raku) combines pane creation, literal input, control-mode observation and screen capture. It filters a snapshot with query data and a Raku predicate, then compares an exact source query with the captured pane. Its query plan shows where evaluation takes place. ```console $ raku -I. examples/session-workflow.raku ``` The output includes `Session: 2 panes`, `editor: hello from Raku`, and `Owned clients, daemon and socket cleaned up`. ## Recover after a command fails The [batch recovery example](batch-recovery.raku) sets an option, sends an invalid command, and checks that the following command was skipped. It verifies the first effect and removes it explicitly. ```console $ raku -I. examples/batch-recovery.raku ``` It reports `Complete`, `Failed` and `Skipped` outcomes, followed by `Recovery: removed the first effect explicitly` and `Owned daemon and socket cleaned up`. A failed batch does not undo commands that already succeeded. ## Select a tmux executable Every program except the minimal quickstart accepts `--tmux`. For that quickstart, select the supported binary through `PATH`. The repository's [example check](../tools/check-examples.raku) selects `LIBTMUX_TEST_TMUX` through a private temporary `PATH`, checks displayed source against these files, runs all programs, checks their results, and rejects leftover owned socket directories. See [Contributing](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks) for validation.

# tmux compatibility

Status: accepted.

## Decision

Support Linux and the declared stable tmux releases from 3.3a through 3.8.
Use the daemon's version and observed capabilities when selecting commands,
fields, codecs and layouts. A newer client executable does not upgrade the
daemon. Unknown and vendor releases require an explicit support decision.

Keep release profiles in [LibTmux::Catalogue](../../lib/LibTmux/Catalogue.rakumod).
Each profile names its upstream commit. The oldest and newest profiles define
the required live CI jobs; intermediate releases retain pure compatibility
fixtures. Feature boundaries and known defects belong in the field catalogue.

## Rationale

Runtime checks and CI must agree on supported releases. Typed release records
provide one source for both without a separate configuration format. CI verifies
the fetched tag against the pinned commit; it does not need a second inventory
of individual source-file hashes.

Adding a supported release requires reviewing its feature and defect policies,
updating its profile, and passing the relevant fixtures and endpoint tests.
